messages:
samir: kicking off a privilege census for Q3 — goal: identify orphaned admin grants, stale KMS key bindings, and high-risk service-account roles. aiming for a lightweight remediation runbook by end of next week. link to sheet: https://go/reports/priv-census-q3
elaine: +1. scope? include dedicated infra projects + any 3rd-party integrations we manage keys for?
samir: yes to infra projects and 3P. prioritize prod-facing projects first. low-risk dev projects can be second wave.
zoe: can we get a quick query for ownerless IAM principals? throwing something into the sheet helps automation.
cj: pasted a starter GCP query in the sheet earlier — here's an AWS assume-role check for orphan detection:
```
aws iam list-roles --query 'Roles[?RoleLastUsed.LastUsedDate==`null` || RoleLastUsed.LastUsedDate<`2024-01-01`].{RoleName:RoleName}'
```
cj: we'll refine thresholds. also recommend checking KMS key policies for principals that are not in the SSO org.
tony: for KMS specifically, we should look at both key policy and the grant table. grants can persist even after the IAM binding is removed.
elaine: good call. sec-bot: can you run an initial scan and dump results to #sec-artifacts?
sec-bot: scan queued — estimated finish 35m. results will include: orphaned roles, keys with external principals, svcacct keys with >90d last-use. (reaction :eyes:)
zoe: FYI — we should treat service accounts used by pipelines as special: coordinate with infra to avoid breaking deploys. mark them as "do-not-delete" in the sheet if confirmed.
samir: action items: 1) sec-bot scan -> #sec-artifacts (cj) 2) manual review for top-25 highest-priv principals (elaine, zoe) 3) create remediation runbook + rollback steps (tony) 4) communicate maintenance window for destructive remediations (ops)
elaine: i'll take the top-25 and annotate owners. if no owner found, propose timeboxed disable then delete after 7 days.
tony: runbook notes: always take KMS key snapshot (backup key metadata and policy), revoke grants via API, monitor CloudTrail/KMS logs for retries for 48h post-change. include a quick restore command in runbook.

Examples for KMS policy snapshot:
```
gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy KEY_NAME --location=global --keyring=RING_NAME > key-policy-KEY_NAME.json
```

elaine: approval flow? for keys that touch prod, we need at least one approver from infra + one from product-security. recommend a 24h SLA for approvals so we don't stall.

cj: i'll wire an approval checkbox into the sheet and hook the pipeline to require both checkboxes before destructive ops.

zoe: risk note: some older runtime tasks assume admin roles; i'll scan gen logs for "AccessDenied" spikes after test disables.

samir: timeline: scan now, triage within 48h, dry-run remediations in staging next week, prod remediations the week after (with maintenance windows).

ops: schedule windows for next Tue/Wed mornings PST; ops will post calendar invites once owners are set.

elaine: any objections to the 7-day quarantine before deletion? gives teams a rollback window.

tony: 7 days fine, but for keys used by critical infra consider 14 days. document case-by-case exceptions.

samir: final: please add your name next to any resource you claim in the sheet by EOD today. i'll post a summary to #leadership tomorrow. thanks all. (reaction :thumbsup:)
